title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל הזקן

paragraphs:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel the Elder. He too was nasi, in the year 3810, eighteen years before the destruction. He was killed at the destruction, one of the Ten Martyrs of the kingdom; concerning this it says, “The lot fell upon Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.” See R' Yishmael ben Elisha the high priest. He is not mentioned in the Mishnah. Some say that he is the one mentioned in the first chapter of Avot, “Shimon his son says.” Tosafot Yom Tov likewise writes on Avot, mishnah 16: “Rabban Gamliel says” means Rabban Gamliel the Elder, son of R' Shimon son of Hillel the Elder. In the siddur commentary the two words “Shimon son” are missing. In mishnah 17: “Shimon his son says, ‘All my days ….’” At the end of the first chapter of Keritut, 8a, R' Shimon said, “By this Dwelling!” Rashi explains it as an oath. Rashbam, Bava Batra 166a, explains that he swore by the Temple. Thus he cannot be the Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel mentioned afterward, “The world stands on three things,” who did not live in the Temple period. But the one who spoke in Keritut, when bird-offering pairs cost gold dinars, saying, “By this Dwelling! I shall not pass this night until they cost dinars,” must have lived in the Temple period. He is the one who was killed, not the Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel who was Rabbi's father. He was not called “Rabban Shimon his son” because he was young when he said this and had not attained the distinction of Rabban. Tosafot Yom Tov writes thus, with different wording; I have also written some wording from Sefer Yuhasin. Nahalat Shimoni erred.

Asarah Ma'amarot, Hakor Din, part 2, chapter 19, writes likewise. Therefore, immediately at the end of the first chapter of Avot it says, “Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says”—he is the son of Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh, Rabbi's father—“On three things ….” Therefore Rabbi placed his own words in Avot, chapter 2, “Rabbi says, ‘What is the upright path …?’” next to his father's words at the end of the first chapter. Afterward he arranged his son's words: “Rabban Gamliel son of R' Yehudah the Nasi says, ‘Torah study is fine …’”; see his entry. After him it says, “Do not separate yourself from the community,” which Hillel said: he is his grandson, the brother of R' Yehudah the Nasi. They ceased styling the patriarchs Rabban, instead using R' Yehudah the Nasi. He—Rabban Gamliel son of Rabbi—had a son called R' Hillel, who became nasi after him; with him the patriarchate ceased. He instituted the system of intercalation. Rabbi placed the words of Hillel, his grandson, nearby to fulfill concerning himself, “They shall not depart from your mouth, from the mouth of your seed, and from the mouth of your seed's seed.” This disagrees with Abarbanel and the commentators, who think that this Hillel is Hillel the Elder. Afterward he placed next to this Hillel the words of Hillel the Elder, “An ignorant person does not fear sin …,” rather than “He used to say,” as in the commentators' reading of “Hillel says, ‘Do not separate yourself,’” whom they take to be Hillel the Elder. Those who read “He used to say, ‘On three things the world stands,’” and delete Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel likewise err, because they think he is the Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel mentioned previously. This is not so: the earlier one is the martyred Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, son of Rabban Gamliel the Elder; this one is Rabbi's father. See his entry and Yad Yehudah, no. 37; Abarbanel also writes thus.

In Bava Batra 166a another text reads, “R' Gamliel said, ‘By this Dwelling!’” Our reading and that of Torat Kohanim, Tazria, are: “Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said, ‘By this Dwelling! I shall not pass the night ….’” In Arakhin 10, end of side b: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel taught, “The Shiloah used to flow …”; “Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says, ‘There were no הרדולים [provisionally hydraules] in the Temple ….’” It appears to be this Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. Nahalat Shimoni erred. In the Mishnah, Ketubbot 59b, R' Eliezer says that even if she brought him a hundred maidservants, he compels her to work in wool, because idleness, and so forth. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says that one who vows that his wife shall not work must divorce her, and so forth. There, 61b, R' Malkiyo said, “The halakhah follows R' Eliezer.” Tosafot write: “The halakhah follows R' Eliezer”—but do we not hold that wherever Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel teaches in our Mishnah, the halakhah follows him? This is not that one who lived in R' Eliezer's days. End of quotation. Thus in Tosafot's view it appears that the Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel who disputes R' Eliezer in the Mishnah is not Rabbi's father, whom the halakhah follows everywhere in the Mishnah. If so, he is the son of Rabban Gamliel the Elder and is mentioned in the Mishnah. But Rosh, no. 27, writes that this is not much proof: the ruling follows R' Eliezer where he disputes the first tanna, but where he disputes Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, wherever the latter teaches, the halakhah follows him. Thus this Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is Rabbi's father, son of Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh.

They said concerning Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: when he rejoiced at the Water-Drawing celebration, he would take eight flaming torches, throw one and catch another, and they did not touch each other. When he bowed, he planted his two thumbs on the ground, bent down and kissed the pavement, and rose upright. No other creature could do this; this is kiddah: Sukkah 53a. Nahalat Shimoni erred. In Sotah 49b: “There were a thousand children in my father's house, and none remained except me and my father's brother's son in Asia.” Tosafot, Avodah Zarah, chapter 2, 32, end of side a, write that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel the Elder said this. Nahalat Shimoni did not know these words of Tosafot. See there in Tosafot what they write about which Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel reported in R' Yehoshua Kapusai's name. In Avodah Zarah 20a: he stood on a step of the Temple Mount, saw an exceptionally beautiful gentile woman, and said, “How manifold are Your works, O Lord!” Nahalat Shimoni erred. Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh was his son.
